findings.title: Etheric embodiment and hearing before the ear
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places dreamlike astral image consciousness before entry into etheric materiality. External etheric vibration then yields an organism-wide precursor of hearing before a separate organ exists.

findings.title: Reproduction, death and perceptual differentiation
findings.paraphrase: With condensation, reproduction changes from division to a locally mediated process, and the remaining body may disintegrate. Hearing localizes while touch still belongs to most of the body. Section 6 names the two early stages after the description of reproduction and death.

findings.title: External sunlight and the first eye rudiments
findings.paraphrase: Part of the light ether is withdrawn at solar separation and subsequently acts from outside. Steiner relates this altered dependence to the first organs receptive to sunlight, followed by further densification and the fire-mist human constitution. The chapter itself gives relative order, while Hyperborean placement is an editorial crosswalk.

findings.title: Reproductive force redirected to inward organs
findings.paraphrase: Steiner pictures older and newer reproductive forms coexisting. He connects density with redirecting part of the prior reproductive capacity into inward organs, mentioning the brain as an instrument of inwardly acquired cognition. He distinguishes early incomplete formation from readiness for spirit contact around mid-Lemuria.

findings.title: Mobility and senses before division into sexes
findings.paraphrase: In the late pre-division account, movement organs are comparatively developed. Hearing and touch are present earlier than light perception, which develops later in the life described. The text also situates extra-parental maturation and externally supplied heat before the later reproductive organization.

findings.title: Two forms of spiritual influence on early humanity
findings.paraphrase: Steiner assigns regulation of reproduction to advanced beings acting on the majority as instinct. A separate, less advanced group directs inner images toward the sensory environment, interrupting what he describes as an otherwise dreamlike spiritual life.

findings.title: Fire mist, upright form and divided guidance
findings.paraphrase: Thinking organs are prepared in the fire mist. After lunar separation and cooling, Steiner links upstanding posture and hand rudiments with altered functions of the upper body. He assigns lower-body guidance to Moon beings and renewed influence over developed personality to Luciferic beings.

findings.title: Moon separation, form and generation
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes the withdrawal of hardening forces as making individual embodiment possible. It relates emerging sexual differentiation to the distribution of seed and quickening capacities and describes lunar forces continuing from outside Earth.

findings.title: Breath, warmth and early bodily systems
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 attributes guidance of breath into the body to Sun beings. It distinguishes warmth currents as beginnings of blood circulation from an internal differentiation of air as a basis of the later nervous system. These are claimed antecedents, with no implication of modern anatomical completion.

findings.title: Interrupted embodiment, I and return
findings.paraphrase: Some souls can no longer inhabit hardening forms and continue elsewhere. Spirits of Form kindle the I, whose experience carries into body-free existence. As suitable forms become available after Moon separation, formerly displaced souls return over a long interval. The account distinguishes these first returns from repeat Earth incarnations.

findings.title: Lunar organization and two adverse influences
findings.paraphrase: The Moon beings shape the relation of I and bodies. Luciferic intervention grants greater control of consciousness images alongside error and dependence on astral impulses. Steiner separately introduces Ahrimanic influence through earthly forces and fear before its stronger mid-Atlantean manifestation.

findings.title: Different nighttime agencies act concurrently
findings.paraphrase: With alternating day and night, Steiner differentiates the nighttime sphere of activity around I and astral body from the simultaneous activity around physical and life bodies. Spirits of Form are common to both lists. This describes an early Earth rhythm, with a specific allocation of agencies rather than exclusive builders.

findings.title: Will, memory, speech and differentiated guidance
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 describes will-directed schooling and temple practice, and connects late Lemurian memory and elementary moral concepts to an account of women's role and of rhythmic utterance. The source uses gender essentialism and evolutionary ranking. Its local continuity claim reaches into early Atlantis while the fourth subgroup is in preparation.

findings.title: Volcanic destruction and a quieter precursor settlement
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 depicts volcanism destroying Lemurian territory while a relatively quiet area supports settlement and formation of an Atlantean precursor group. The account distinguishes the destructive environment from development in the refuge.

findings.title: Overlapping phases and memory-led naming
findings.paraphrase: Subgroups in Steiner's early taxonomy persist alongside successors. The first named subgroup emphasizes retained sense impressions, attachment to past experience and the development of naming already incipient in late Lemuria.

findings.title: Second phase and shared memory of deeds
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes remembered personal achievement as a new basis of leadership and ancestor veneration. Recalled joint undertakings could bind groups in addition to ties of descent.

findings.title: Third phase, inherited authority and experimental settlement
findings.paraphrase: The third phase consolidates communal institutions, transmits leadership across generations, and uses remembered experience and experiments when establishing communities. Steiner sees an opening for personal appropriation of nature powers in the same process.

findings.title: Fourth and fifth phases change the role of power
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places intensified egoistic use of life forces in the fourth phase and the use of comparison and judgment to regulate desire in the fifth. He describes a tradeoff between inward combinatory thought and immediate command of living forces.

findings.title: Sixth and seventh phases differ in uses of thinking
findings.paraphrase: The sixth phase applies thinking more broadly to social order and law. The seventh is depicted as retaining greater attachment to inherited memory and belief in life powers while also developing thought. The source's extension of this typology to living populations is unsupported racial stereotyping.

findings.title: Pictorial memory, education and seed-force technology
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 presents imitation and remembered cases as a basis of judgment and education, with initiates treated separately. It claims growth forces in seeds could be redirected to devices under different environmental conditions. These are esoteric technological claims without archaeological or physical verification.

findings.title: Planetary affinities, sleep and distinct oracle practices
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 places the fuller differentiation of planetary affiliations in Atlantis. It distinguishes what sleepers and different kinds of initiates could experience through portions of the life-body, and calls the Christ oracle a prophetic stream within this wider field.

findings.title: Bodily stabilization and the mid-Atlantean crisis
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 connects bodily stabilization with variable plasticity, while naming misuse of growth and reproductive powers, including by some initiates, as a cause of destructive air and water changes. It separately emphasizes Ahrimanic distortion of sensory and postmortem experience from mid-Atlantis.

findings.title: Oracle preservation and the brain as instrument of thought
findings.paraphrase: The Sun oracle is credited with keeping and passing on etheric patterns of initiates. Among a successor group Steiner describes closer physical–etheric union, diminished older memory and the transformation of the brain into a needed instrument of thought and bodily self-awareness.

findings.title: Manu, independent understanding and a new type of initiate
findings.paraphrase: GA 11 describes selection of an eastward successor group, spiritual ideas addressed to its own thinking, and training of earthly thinkers as initiates. Later communities take on different forms as that teaching blends with older local inheritances.

findings.title: Two catastrophe narratives have distinct claimed mechanisms
findings.paraphrase: The Lemurian transition is connected to I-related use of fire under Luciferic influence. The Atlantean transition is linked to misuse of growth and generation under different conditions, with air and water effects and further migration. Both accounts are Steiner's esoteric prehistory.

findings.title: Atlantean inheritance, teachers and cultural overlap
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes the seven disciples of the Christ-initiate teaching people receptive to residual Atlantean perception. It explicitly distinguishes those people from later historical India and lets Indian cultural development continue concurrently with the next two dominant periods. Its claims about caste and spiritual descent belong to a historical esoteric account.

findings.title: Etheric emphasis in the individual-development stream
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 assigns etheric development to the earliest post-Atlantean individual in its second current, alongside an independent account of the age at which natural maturing ceases. This is a typological emphasis and has no bearing on established human biology.

findings.title: Persian orientation to work on Earth and the spirits of light
findings.paraphrase: Steiner portrays the sensory world as a field of action charged with spiritual significance. He distinguishes his primordial Zarathustra from later bearers of the name and associates the teaching about light with resisting Ahrimanic influence after death.

findings.title: The sentient body in the individual-development stream
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 assigns the sentient body to the second cultural period at the scale of typical individual development. The passage separately assigns the sentient soul to the following period at that same scale.

findings.title: Different initiatory responses to sensory immersion
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes related but distinct Egyptian and Chaldean-Babylonian cultural settings and ties increasing sensory interests to changing experience after death. Hermes is credited with preparing people during earthly life for the spiritual world, within Steiner's account of declining postmortem vision.

findings.title: Celestial observation and the Pergamum image
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 describes Chaldean observation of star motions as recognition of an intelligible pattern in visible nature. Pergamum represents this cultural period in the lecture's interpretive scheme.

findings.title: Sentient soul in one stream and a later analogy in another
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 assigns the sentient soul to the Egyptian-Chaldean period in its individual stream. In the separate whole-humanity stream, Steiner also calls fifth-age humanity analogous to the individual age band he associates with that same soul member.

findings.title: First Greco-Roman subperiod and inward independence
findings.paraphrase: GA 181 marks a first subperiod around 747 to 27 BCE. Steiner describes waning felt membership in a spiritual cosmos and connects more self-contained human experience with Greek culture. He presents the subsequent Christ event and secular culture as concurrent currents.

findings.title: Second Greco-Roman subperiod and dogmatic reception
findings.paraphrase: In a middle subperiod approximately 27 BCE to 693 CE, Steiner interprets the spread of external Christian doctrine as concurrent with difficulty understanding the Christ event through immediate cognition. This is the lecture's interpretation of church history.

findings.title: Third Greco-Roman subperiod and the split of faith and knowledge
findings.paraphrase: For the period approximately 693 to 1413 CE, GA 181 describes a separation between knowing by human concepts and accepting supersensible matters under revelatory authority. The boundary dates are approximate and the characterization concerns Steiner's European narrative.

findings.title: Golgotha as a second current within the cultural sequence
findings.paraphrase: GA 201 describes a continuous succession of cultures and a second current entering it at Golgotha, with its own proposed time symmetry. The historical sequence supplies the setting. Steiner assigns the Christ event a distinct spiritual origin.

findings.title: Golgotha, the I and the after-death world
findings.paraphrase: Steiner contrasts the cultivated visibility of spirit in Greek art with a shadowy postmortem experience. He places Moses among preparations for the highest form of the I, and credits the Christ event with limiting Ahriman's activity in the realm of the dead.

findings.title: Older and newer initiation overlap
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes residual natural supersensible faculties among some initiates during and beyond the fourth period. It also describes a newer way of developing cognition through human understanding and feeling, in which the Christ mysteries become central.

findings.title: Three concurrent scales of soul development
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 distinguishes humanity-wide maturation, the individual development of the consciousness soul, and a third current attributed to peoples. The first current is likened to the span in which an individual develops the sentient soul. The lecture's national character generalizations are historically situated and unsupported as descriptions of present peoples.

findings.title: Conscious social insight in the consciousness-soul age
findings.paraphrase: Steiner asks listeners to notice the human labor behind an everyday purchase and to revisit their own past from a more objective standpoint. He presents these exercises as ways to counter isolation and deliberately cultivate interest in other people.

findings.title: Long preparation, fifteenth-century start and later acceleration
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes preparation beginning in late antiquity, gradual emergence in the twelfth to fourteenth centuries, clearer emergence in the fifteenth, and rapid acceleration of intellectual development from the sixteenth. These thresholds describe different stages of one transition.

findings.title: Transformation of the third period's insights
findings.paraphrase: Steiner forecasts that what the third culture perceived dimly will recur in a form integrated with personal intelligence, feeling and the Christ mystery. The fifth and sixth periods are presented as especially consequential for this work.

findings.title: Etheric Christ and the exercise of free will
findings.paraphrase: GA 186 projects a reappearance of Christ in etheric experience and relates the response to voluntary spiritual action. It contrasts a misuse of the same powers that would bind activity to physicality. This is a teaching and prediction attributed to Steiner.

findings.title: The sixth culture begins as a possibility during the fifth
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 says the next period is slowly prepared during the current one. It projects a fuller accord between material civilization and spiritual life, anticipated wherever spiritual understanding is brought to sensory experience.

findings.title: A transformed Persian recurrence
findings.paraphrase: GA 106 describes a future cultural revival of the Zarathustra current in transformed circumstances. The recurrence is a correspondence between periods in Steiner's teaching, without a prediction that the specific institutions of historical Zoroastrianism return unchanged.

findings.title: Philadelphia and the transformation of wisdom into love
findings.paraphrase: In GA 104 the spiritual wisdom cultivated during the fifth cultural period is supposed to become an impulse of love in the sixth. Philadelphia signifies brotherly love, before the culmination of the seventh culture and the subsequent war.

findings.title: A transformed first-period pattern in the seventh culture
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes an altered recurrence of ancient Indian culture. The social analogy in §14 contrasts inherited authority with future grouping under different conditions. It does not justify caste hierarchy or ranked treatment of contemporary people.

findings.title: Development continues as opportunities change
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 describes continued development in the seventh culture for souls prepared in the fifth and sixth, and more difficult conditions for others until a later time. A further upheaval comes after this cultural sequence.

findings.title: Earth epochs nested inside the physical form condition
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 places the seven great Earth epochs inside the fourth form stage of Earth's fourth condition of life, numbered 172 in this lecture. The seven post-Atlantean cultures belong to the fifth of those Earth epochs. The local 3–4–4 tally refers to completed subdivisions at three depths.

findings.title: Seals follow a transition beyond the seventh culture
findings.paraphrase: The lecture locates Philadelphia within the present set of cultural periods, the War of All Against All after that set, and the seven seals after the war. The seals and trumpets each have their own further division in this particular account.

findings.title: The first five seals and transformed cultural fruits
findings.paraphrase: GA 104a uses horse-and-rider pictures for the first four postwar periods, relating them to the first four cultures. The fifth period is pictured through the white robe and an astral body illuminated by the I. The source marks a gap at the end of the discussion of the fifth seal.

findings.title: Philadelphia and the sixth seal occupy different scales
findings.paraphrase: The lecture moves between a prewar cultural period associated with Philadelphia, its projected interventions in air and light, and an image of their fruits at the sixth seal. The claim that electrical waves and moral actions will cause earthquakes is unsupported.

findings.title: Trumpets and the ascent beyond physical form
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 places the seven trumpet subdivisions after the seals. It describes passage beyond the trumpets through astral and two Devachanic degrees, followed by densification into the next condition of life. This later Earth condition of life is at a different scale from Future Jupiter.

findings.title: Larynx, breath and the post-trumpet astral image
findings.paraphrase: Steiner takes the larynx and incoming breath as an example in his apocalyptic interpretation of bodily organs leaving astral forms. The claim belongs to his spiritual forecast and supplies no evidence for anatomical development or physiological function.

findings.title: Post-catastrophe choice, altered conditions and distant lunar work
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 projects seven periods after the convulsion and treats prior choices as preparation for altered spiritual conditions. It then describes lunar return and transformative assistance farther ahead, without supplying the seal-by-seal concordance or dating lunar return to a specific seal.

findings.title: Period arithmetic and the precision of calendar labels
findings.paraphrase: GA 184 calculates 2,160 years from its two stated epoch boundaries and obtains a midpoint by halving the interval. This supports the period length as Steiner's arithmetic convention. Dates obtained by projecting the interval onto other cultures are editorial derivatives, with a calendar-year-zero ambiguity around the BCE/CE crossover.

findings.title: The modern turning point in historical symptomatology
findings.paraphrase: GA 185 distinguishes the early-fifteenth-century change of soul life from familiar markers used in ordinary periodization. It connects late medieval social forms and universalist church life with the preceding period. This is a lecture interpretation of European social history.

findings.title: Early soul-member differentiation and the I
findings.paraphrase: GA 13 distinguishes an early Earth differentiation of sentient, intellectual and consciousness soul in the astral constitution from the culmination that allows the Spirits of Form to kindle the I. Its German §77 names Bewusstseinsseele where the Adams translation uses spiritual soul.

findings.title: The sevenfold pattern loosens and intersecting cycles remain in use
findings.paraphrase: In the 1924 priests' lecture Steiner says numerical regularity begins to shift with the consciousness-soul age. He still uses a seven-part archangelic cycle intersecting the longer cultural periods. The archive's §12 is printed in German in this English source view.

findings.title: Samael, Gabriel and Michael cross the cultural boundary
findings.paraphrase: Steiner names Oriphiel, Anael, Zachariel, Raphael, Samael, Gabriel and Michael in sequence from the time of Golgotha. Samael is already active at the beginning of the fifth culture. The lecture places Gabriel's cycle around 1471 and Michael's around 1879. It assigns longer cycles to beings of the middle hierarchy.

findings.title: Michael and the Christ event from two vantage points
findings.paraphrase: Steiner juxtaposes arrival of Christ on Earth with the farewell experienced by Michael's hosts on the Sun. Michael's later age signifies following Christ's descent, with a future role preceding Christ's deeds on Earth.

findings.title: War of All Against All as a moral transition
findings.paraphrase: The 1924 lecture places the war between great Earth epochs five and six, after cultures six and seven within the fifth. Steiner gives the moral catastrophe primacy and describes accompanying natural events as secondary. The comparison with ice-age events belongs to his teaching.

findings.title: Ephesus also symbolizes the Oriphiel interval
findings.paraphrase: Steiner can use the same church imagery for intersecting archangelic ages. Ephesus is associated here with the first smaller cycle, contemporary with the beginnings of Christianity. This supplies a second association alongside GA 104 III's first cultural period.

findings.title: The fifth-phase migration and bodily self-awareness
findings.paraphrase: This lecture begins an eastward migration in the fifth Atlantean phase, calls the formation of a successor group a last-third process, and connects physical–etheric change with capacity for first-person self-awareness. It also contains unsupported claims about ancestry and present-day populations.

findings.title: I-work on the astral body begins in dim consciousness
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 begins partially unconscious activity of the I on the astral body in Lemuria and early Atlantis, yielding what this translation calls the sensory soul. Later application of the I to other members is treated in the same lecture as a sequence.

findings.title: Etheric and physical work extend over later Atlantean phases
findings.paraphrase: The lecture places dim I-work on the etheric body during Atlantis, giving rise to the intellectual soul, and work on the physical body from the last third, giving rise to the consciousness soul. It associates the fuller individual impulse with Christ and distinguishes it from preliminary self-awareness.

findings.title: Completion of conscious astral transformation and the last trumpet
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes present beginnings of Manas from advanced spiritual self-development at the end of physical Earth. He connects survival into the astralized Earth with transformed etheric organization and interprets Pauline imagery in that context.

findings.title: Angels mediate individual and collective work
findings.paraphrase: GA 121 distinguishes individual work across incarnations from collective impulses. It describes Angels mediating between individual people and Archangels, with Spirits of Personality introducing a further influence at the scale of an age. The lecture's national character and ancestry claims are unsupported.

findings.title: Early Earth bodily currents and preparatory organ forms
findings.paraphrase: Steiner describes etheric humans condensing into mineral-bearing bodies and claims Earth's prior currents continue inward as blood vessels and nerves. He treats the modern umbilical cord as an analogue of a former bond with Earth and names preparatory forms of heart and brain. These are esoteric analogies and developmental claims.

findings.title: Atlantean heart rudiment in the lion group-soul account
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 connects a heart rudiment that later becomes the physical heart with the lion group-soul image. The lecture calls the condensed physical expression of an etheric pattern a horn. The source supplies an Atlantean bodily threshold in its own framework.

findings.title: Old Saturn heart germ in the Leo-region account
findings.paraphrase: GA 110 associates the initial heart germ with the arrest of motion in Old Saturn warmth and the Leo direction, naming activity of Thrones, Seraphim and Cherubim. The breastplate and Cancer discussion is adjacent and refers to a different structure.

findings.title: The I enters the intellectual soul around 333 in a 1924 account
findings.paraphrase: Steiner places an entry of the I into the intellectual soul around 333 CE, and reads the Arius–Athanasius controversy as an external expression. The lecture also phrases an interval as 333 years after Golgotha, leaving its calendar convention to be compared across editions. His reading is a spiritual interpretation of church history.

findings.title: Inherited conditions and the Christ impulse within individual life
findings.paraphrase: Steiner distinguishes inherited father-line impulses from a Christ or Son impulse that he says can be received through the soul within a person's earthly life. The latter belongs to the individual's development and operates at a different scale from a cultural period.

findings.title: Human spiritual fruits prepare Future Jupiter
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 compares Earth's previous preparation of bodily forms with the future formative influence of what people accomplish through soul and etheric transformation. This concerns preparation during spiritualized Earth for its future planetary condition.

findings.title: The fifth Atlantean phase and first I-soul impulse
findings.paraphrase: GA 104 distinguishes the first four phases in its group-soul account from the fifth, where it locates a first impulse toward individualized I-soul. It later reuses their animal-head imagery in its apocalyptic treatment, with an altered meaning.

dossiers.title: Etheric emergence and earliest responsiveness
dossiers.analysis: GA 11 VIII changes the reference point from preterrestrial astral life to etheric embodiment. Its hearing analogy describes a whole-body function.

dossiers.title: Differentiation of body and environment
dossiers.analysis: GA 11 VIII groups the first two epochs in one retrospective account. Its gradual cosmic separation in §10 should be read alongside the more detailed order in IX–X.

dossiers.title: Embodiment, differentiation and new inward powers
dossiers.analysis: GA 11 supplies descriptions of pre-division anatomy, local group development and a volcanic transition. GA 13 relates form, I, lunar withdrawal and agency without supplying a calendar.

dossiers.title: Memory, organization, independent thinking and transition
dossiers.analysis: Read the seven overlapping phases in GA 11 III alongside the broad account of altered life-body, oracle and sensory experience in GA 13 IV. The sources provide no exact alignment for every process.

dossiers.title: Post-Atlantean Earth epoch
dossiers.analysis: The seven cultural periods are nested within this Earth epoch. Dates describe Steiner’s typology and some are inferred using his period arithmetic. GA 13 allows cultural continuities across the boundaries.

dossiers.title: Sixth great Earth epoch
dossiers.analysis: GA 104 places the seven seals here after the War of All Against All. GA 104a treats early seals as astral images of transformed cultural fruits and sometimes moves back to the prewar cultures while discussing them.

dossiers.title: Seventh great Earth epoch
dossiers.analysis: The trumpet subdivisions complete the physical-form sequence in GA 104. The lecture then describes further forms on Earth before a later Earth condition of life. A full trumpet-by-trumpet case remains open.

dossiers.title: Ancient Indian cultural period
dossiers.analysis: Preserved Atlantean perception and its teaching provide a baseline for GA 13’s cultural account. The account explicitly distinguishes the first period from later India.

dossiers.title: Ancient Persian cultural period
dossiers.analysis: Earthly work and the visibility of spiritual activity in the sensory world replace earlier emphases in Steiner’s typology. Ancient Persian spiritual content is projected to recur in transformed form in the sixth period.

dossiers.title: Egypto-Chaldean cultural period
dossiers.analysis: Steiner groups several cultural settings in one typology while describing different initiation streams. The fifth culture is said to revisit earlier spiritual content with awakened individual faculties.

dossiers.title: Greco-Roman cultural period
dossiers.analysis: The mind or intellectual soul is the development foregrounded at the individual scale. GA 181 subdivides the period into three approximate intervals. GA 201 traces the cultural and Christological currents through the same time.

dossiers.title: Consciousness-soul cultural period
dossiers.analysis: The age grows out of earlier processes and is marked by an emphasis on consciously cultivated cognition and action. GA 185 assigns the consciousness soul and the sentient-soul analogy to different currents.

dossiers.title: Sixth post-Atlantean cultural period
dossiers.analysis: A projected consolidation of capacities prepared in the fifth. GA 106 connects the period with the transformed Persian current. GA 104 identifies Philadelphia with the growth of brotherly love.

dossiers.title: Seventh post-Atlantean cultural period
dossiers.analysis: A projected final culture within the fifth great Earth epoch. GA 106 compares it with the first period, while GA 13 emphasizes altered developmental opportunities and a subsequent upheaval.

dossiers.title: Old Saturn organ cross-reference
dossiers.analysis: The seven cosmic dossiers remain the primary stage studies. This supplement points to a targeted comparison of the Old Saturn and Atlantean heart accounts.

comparisons.title: Timing and mechanism of reproductive differentiation
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 VI §§2–5 foregrounds densification and redirected soul force. GA 13 IV §§69–70 ties the beginning of structural differentiation to changed forces at Moon departure. An overlapping process is plausible. Exact equivalence of the causal sequences and their wording awaits German comparison. German confirms the separate emphases: GA 11 uses Verdichtung; GA 13 §70 calls the change Anfang der Trennung after lunar departure. The cross-work timing remains open.

comparisons.title: Two placements for Ahrimanic influence
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §88 already connects Ahrimanic beings to fear in early Earth embodiment. IV §97 specifies a further mid-Atlantean distortion of sensory and postmortem experience. Treat the latter as a specific intensification, with the source naming both effects. The German preserves the distinction as well, and §97 expressly refers back to the beings already indicated.

comparisons.title: Brain and thinking organs have several developmental thresholds
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 VI §§8–9 distinguishes incomplete organ formation and readiness for spirit contact. GA 11 X §§3–6 links preparations to the fire mist and later use by Luciferic entities. GA 13 IV §99 links the Atlantean brain as an instrument of thought to physical–etheric union. The texts use different developmental predicates. Exact anatomical equivalence remains open. German distinguishes Anlage and readiness in GA 11 and later names the physische Gehirn in GA 13 §99.

comparisons.title: Early sight rudiments versus developed light perception
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 IX §7 puts first ocular rudiments after Sun separation. VII §3 characterizes light perception as comparatively late in the late pre-division account and later in individual development. Separate an organ rudiment, a function and its timing in a life before attempting an exact crosswalk. German GA 11 IX §7 speaks of Anlagen to the eyes, whereas VII §3 speaks of Lichtwahrnehmung.

comparisons.title: Named Atlantean phase and approximate midpoint
comparisons.comparison: GA 11 III §§16–19 assigns particular changes in misuse and judgment to successive named phases. GA 13 IV §§96–97 places a spreading crisis around mid-Atlantis without naming a subphase. The passages do not themselves identify the fourth GA 11 phase with the midpoint of GA 13.

comparisons.title: Formation of a soul member and its characteristic cultural development
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §77 German names Bewusstseinsseele in early Earth differentiation. GA 185 VIII §§3–7 names fifth-age individual development of the consciousness soul and a concurrent humanity-wide analogy to the sentient soul. Keep early articulation, period emphasis and social typology at their stated scales.

comparisons.title: Calendar conventions and the Christological anchor
comparisons.comparison: GA 181 §2 alternates expressions referring to BCE, Golgotha and the founding of Christianity while giving approximate boundaries. GA 184 uses 747 and 1413 in a simple 2,160-year calculation and GA 201 distinguishes a second temporal scheme at Christ. Preserve the stated numbers as approximate and audit German calendar terminology and modern crossover arithmetic before treating the implied dates as exact.

comparisons.title: Philadelphia, the sixth seal and the sixth great Earth epoch
comparisons.comparison: GA 104 XI §17 assigns Philadelphia to a prewar subperiod. GA 104a II-9 §§10–11 then shifts from that cultural period to its supposed fruit in the sixth seal. Both lectures supply grounds to distinguish the scales. A complete concordance with GA 346 remains open.

comparisons.title: GA 13 and GA 104 stage and attribute formation of the soul members differently
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §77 speaks of early differentiation of the astral body into three soul members before the Spirits of Form kindle the I. GA 104 IX §7 ascribes successive development of the soul members to dim work of the I on astral, etheric and physical bodies from Lemuria through late Atlantis. Germ and subsequent elaboration could account for part of the difference, but the sources do not establish that identification. Compare the German GA 104 and full argument in GA 13 next.

comparisons.title: Two scales for the seven churches
comparisons.comparison: GA 104 III §§15–18 uses Ephesus as a representative of the first post-Atlantean culture. GA 346 VI §§11–14,27 also uses Ephesus for the first archangelic cycle near Golgotha. The latter lecture explicitly names intersecting scales, leaving the correspondences alongside one another.

comparisons.title: Ideal period arithmetic and 1924 qualifications on numerical regularity
comparisons.comparison: GA 184 uses 2,160-year arithmetic for the fourth culture. GA 346 VI §§8–10 says that regular numerical patterns loosen in the consciousness-soul age, while continuing to use related cycles. The latter does not specify a replacement end year for the fifth culture. Derived future labels remain approximate.

comparisons.title: Two heart rudiment accounts share a lion association
comparisons.comparison: GA 110 VIII §§6–8 names an Old Saturn heart rudiment in the Leo direction. GA 104 IX §§20–22 places the rudiment leading to the physical heart within an Atlantean lion group-soul account. An earlier warmth predisposition and a later etheric or physical elaboration are plausible successive thresholds. The passages do not directly identify one as the continuation of the other. Compare the German terminology and GA 110 IX before assigning a single inception.

comparisons.title: Several distinct claims about inception and expression of the I
comparisons.comparison: GA 13 IV §77 describes kindling by Spirits of Form in early terrestrial evolution. GA 104 VIII §§7–8 and IX §20 attach first-person expression or first I-soul impulse to the fifth Atlantean phase. GA 346 VII §3 attaches 333 CE to entry into the intellectual soul. Track the predicates separately. The exact relationship between the two purported firsts still requires direct comparison. The 333 CE expression and the years-after-Golgotha wording in GA 346 VII §14 also merit edition comparison.
